source.title: Connecting Neural Models Latent Geometries with Relative Geodesic Representations
source.authors: Hanlin Yu; Berfin Inal; Georgios Arvanitidis; Søren Hauberg; Francesco Locatello; Marco Fumero

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates representation alignment and interchangeability using relative geodesic retrieval and stitching, rather than measuring convergence with the original claim’s method.
record.gate_note: The paper also compares geodesic approximations with true geodesic energies and reports results for alternative metrics, datasets, anchors, and other settings. Rows below focus on reported outcomes that measure cross-model retrieval or stitching. Results cited from prior work are not included.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a methods paper proposing relative geodesic representations. Its absolute cross-model retrieval and zero-shot stitching results still bear on V4, i.e. whether one model's latent space can be mapped onto another's with little loss. The pairs are autoencoders from different seeds, and ResNet-50, ViT-16, ViT-32 and DINOv2 across architectures and objectives. The comparisons of RelGeo against Rel(Cosine) are method benchmarking, not tests of the claim. No version other than V4 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors assume models trained on similar data parametrize approximately the same manifold, up to bounded distortion. They conclude that relative geodesic representations align and stitch models across seeds, architectures, objectives and, more tentatively, modalities, outperforming prior methods. They note the straight-line approximation can degrade in high-curvature, off-support regions.
record.recipe_differences: Uses pullback-geometric relative geodesic representations and retrieval/stitching evaluations; it does not reproduce a scale-and-capability convergence measurement. The paper cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis as motivation.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported retrieval changes with representation metric or decoder choice, dataset, and in the multimodal appendix with the MRR metric; the study also varies anchor counts, Diet data points, discretization steps, augmentation strength, and anchor-selection scheme.

fits_no_version.finding: RelGeo(Fisher) gives high cross-model stitching accuracy (e.g. CIFAR-10 0.959) but instance retrieval MRR near chance (about 0.01). Task-level stitching can succeed without instance-level alignment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Measured interchangeability depends on whether success is judged by task-level decodability or by instance-level correspondence.

fits_no_version.finding: Relative geodesic representations outperform cosine relative representations in retrieval (Table 1); this is the paper's own method against prior methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Measured cross-model alignment depends on the invariance (similarity function) used to compare latent spaces.

record.problems: No model-scale or capability trend is tested. Retrieval and stitching are indirect measures of alignment rather than direct comparisons of distances between data points. Vision-foundation results are averages over model pairs, and multimodal results do not vary the text model's capability. The paper's stated approximation may be less accurate in high-curvature, out-of-support regions.
record.rows_left_out: No results-bearing conditions from the directly relevant retrieval or stitching tables were omitted. The paper reports many further metric tables, pairwise heatmaps, and ablations in Appendix A.4; these were not separately recorded where they repeat or subdivide the aggregate outcomes already represented here.

untested.parts: No sweep over model scale or capability.
The CLIP text encoder is fixed; there is no test of alignment rising as the vision and language models improve.
Seed pairs of autoencoders are used only for mapping and retrieval; shared features or subspaces versus units are not measured.
No interpretable features or circuits are measured.
Convergence similarity measures, neighbour settings and OOD inputs are not varied; only the paper's own mapping methods vary.
Neither a plateau with scale nor shared data or objectives as the cause of alignment is tested.
Mapping without paired data, and linear or affine stitching layers between foundation models, are not tested; only anchor-based relative representations are.

missing.what: Off-diagonal cross-modal (vision vs CLIP text) MRR values for each pair and method
Same-model (diagonal) stitching accuracies needed as the reference for cross-model accuracy
Autoencoder retrieval MRR against number of anchors, in numbers (0.998 at 50+ anchors)
RelGeo(Fisher) stitching accuracy and MRR aggregates

record.verdict_notes: Primarily a methods paper; most row baselines are competing methods, which is method benchmarking. The V4 evidence comes from absolute cross-model performance against same-model performance. The multimodal aggregate in Table 15 is dominated by intra-modal pairs; the main-text claim of substantial improvement refers to cross-modal values of about 0.1.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep tests whether alignment rises with model scale or capability.
The multimodal experiment evaluates retrieval with a fixed CLIP text encoder and alternative vision encoders; it does not test whether alignment increases as both vision and language models improve.
Autoencoders with different initializations are evaluated for retrieval and stitching, but the study does not directly measure shared features or subspaces.
The study tests relative-geodesic retrieval and stitching, not all listed mapping approaches, and does not test alignment without paired data.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are measured.
The study compares representation metrics and datasets, but does not test out-of-distribution inputs or the effect of varying the number of neighbours.
Some measured alignment is incomplete, but the study does not test whether alignment plateaus with scale or whether shared data or objectives cause it.
